subject: PO signal: aligning vendor form fields, itemization conventions, and issuance SLA
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@starkplatform.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PO signal: aligning vendor form fields, itemization conventions, and issuance SLA

Hi Lina —

Following our kickoff earlier this week, attaching a short checklist and our PO template so we can align on the fields and expected cadence for PO issuance. Goal: avoid back-and-forth on invoice acceptance once SOW is signed. Please confirm the items below and flag any constraints on your side.

Quick checklist (what we need to confirm from vendor):
- Legal vendor name and remit address (exact text for PO)
- Tax identifier (TIN / VAT) and remit country
- Preferred invoice email and AP contact (name + email + phone)
- Bank details or portal for ACH/wire (if required before first invoice)
- Insurance certificate (if applicable) and W-9 / W-8 (US vendors)

PO-specific fields we require on every PO (must be present):
- PO number (Redwood will generate)
- Billing party (vendor legal name)
- Line-item SKU or item code (vendor can map to your internal SKU)
- Short description (1-2 lines)
- Quantity, unit price, unit of measure
- Start / end dates for services or subscription periods
- GL/Cost center code (we provide when we issue PO)
- Deliverable / milestone reference (if tied to SOW)

Line-item structure guidance (our conventions):
- Professional Services: one line per milestone (e.g., PS-M1: Integration; qty=1; unit price = milestone amount).
- Subscription / Compute: itemize by SKU and billing period (monthly/quarterly). If you have meter-based charges, include an example line with estimated monthly qty.
- Third-party pass-throughs: list as separate line items with vendor name in description.

Timeline and SLA for PO issuance:
- New vendors (first PO): 7 business days from signed SOW + completed onboarding docs.
- Existing vendors with active profile: 2 business days.
- If any compliance exceptions are needed (e.g., custom tax handling), add 3–5 business days.

Attachments included: Redwood_PO_Template_v2.xlsx (fillable columns mirror fields above), vendor-onboarding-questionnaire.pdf.

Ask: Please review and reply with any fields you cannot provide or any internal naming conventions that differ (e.g., if you cannot expose a SKU, tell us how you prefer to map). If okay, confirm vendor legal name and AP contact and we’ll schedule PO issuance after SOW countersigned.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Strategic Procurement (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@starkplatform.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@starkplatform.com
Date: 2027-03-14T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO signal: aligning vendor form fields, itemization conventions, and issuance SLA

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear checklist and template. A few quick questions from our side before we confirm: 

1) GL/Cost center: we can include an internal cost center but we usually rely on the buyer to populate the GL on their side. If you require a GL in the PO body, can Redwood accept it as an optional column and still process invoices if it's empty?

2) Tax id: we're a US entity (Stark Platform, Inc., EIN 12-3456789). For our EU branch (if you ever route to EU remit), the VAT sits under a different legal entity — we'll flag that if/when needed.

3) Bundled services: we typically bill integrations as a single line with a breakdown in an attachment. Will that be acceptable, or do you require each sub-task as its own PO line?

4) Sample filled PO: can you attach one filled example (one for a services milestone and one for a subscription) so our billing team sees expected mapping?

We can provide the insurance cert and W-9 by end of day Friday.

Best,
Lina Gomez
Vendor Operations Lead
Stark Platform

Hi Lina —

Thanks — quick answers inline to help your billing team: 

1) GL/Cost center: We will always generate and include an internal GL/cost center on the PO. It is okay for you to leave your GL column blank; Redwood will not reject invoices solely because a vendor-side GL is missing. We prefer that vendors leave a vendor_sku column so we can match items programmatically.

2) Tax: noted on the US EIN — thanks. If we ever route to an EU remit, we'll request the specific legal entity and VAT at that time. No action needed now.

3) Bundled services: Preferred approach is one PO line per milestone for professional services (easier for revenue recognition). If you must bill as one bundled line, include an invoice appendix that maps subcomponents to amounts. That appendix should be referenced in the PO deliverable field. Both are acceptable, but milestone lines are preferred.

4) Sample filled PO: attaching a filled example for both a milestone and a subscription row. See attached file Redwood_PO_Template_v2_filled_example.xlsx — it includes two example lines: 
- PS-M1 (Integration): qty=1, unit price=USD 18,000, deliverable ref=SOW Section 2.1
- SUB-COMPUTE-1000 (Compute credits): qty=1000, unit price=USD 0.05, billing period=monthly

PO issuance timeline nuance: for new legal entities we need completed onboarding + bank verification; that typically stretches the 7 business days to 9–10. If you can expedite bank verification (upload portal), we can keep to 7.

Next steps: can you confirm (a) preferred invoice email, (b) AP contact, and (c) whether you want milestone lines or a bundled invoice appendix as your default? Once we have those, Evelyn will queue the PO issuance after SOW signature.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_PO_Template_v2_filled_example.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Lina —

Appreciate the quick responses and the W-9 ETA. Confirming next steps and timeline from Redwood:

- Upload insurance and W-9 to the vendor portal (link below) to avoid hold-ups on bank verification.
- We will queue the PO for issuance after SOW countersign and completed onboarding docs. For Stark Platform as a new vendor, anticipate PO in 7–9 business days if the portal items are complete; 2 business days for future orders once profile is active.

Meeting: I’m scheduling a quick 20-minute alignment call on Thursday 3/18 at 10:00am PT to walk through the template and ensure your billing team sees the example mapping. Invite to follow.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this operational.

Best,
